text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "eligibility/rules.py defines QUALIFYING_SCORE = 60 and PREGNANCY_QUALIFYING_SCORE = 45. threshold_for(household: Household) -> int returns PREGNANCY_QUALIFYING_SCORE if has_pregnant_member(household) else QUALIFYING_SCORE, so the cutoff a near-miss must be within 5 points of depends on pregnancy status.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "is_eligible(household: Household, score: int | None = None, today=None) -> bool returns False unless household.status == \"active\"; otherwise it computes score = vulnerability_score(household, today) when score is None and returns score >= threshold_for(household). A needs_review function must apply the same active-status gate so inactive/merged households are never flagged.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "has_pregnant_member(household: Household) -> bool is any(m.pregnant for m in household.members); it is the existing helper for the pregnancy branch of the threshold.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "vulnerability_score(household: Household, today=None) -> int in eligibility/scoring.py returns min(100, sum(score_breakdown(household, today).values())); this is the household's vulnerability score the ticket says to use. It accepts an optional today parameter, as does is_eligible.", "file": "eligibility/scoring.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "score_breakdown(household, today=None) computes points from POINTS: child_under_5 = 8 per child capped at 3, elder_over_65 = 10 per elder capped at 2, pregnant = 10, disability = 15, shelter_damaged = 20, income_lost = 15, large_household = 10 if household.size >= 6. Ages come from Member.age_on(day) using completed years, so scores are date-dependent.", "file": "eligibility/scoring.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Household (core/models.py) has status: str = \"active\" (\"active | inactive | merged\"), members: list[Member], size property = len(self.members), and boolean flags shelter_damaged, income_lost, disability. Member has pregnant: bool = False and age_on(day).", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "No function named needs_review or any near-miss/review logic exists in eligibility/ today (search for 'needs_review' and 'near-miss' returned no matches), so this is new code; the closest existing pattern to mirror is is_eligible in eligibility/rules.py.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "tests/test_eligibility.py imports is_eligible, programs, threshold_for from eligibility.rules and score_breakdown, vulnerability_score from eligibility.scoring, and builds households via Household.from_dict with a fixed DAY = date(2026, 3, 10). Edge cases there: a score of 58 (non-pregnant) is not eligible, a score of 45 (pregnant) is eligible — i.e. a non-pregnant household scoring 55-59 and a pregnant household scoring 40-44 are the near-miss bands.", "file": "tests/test_eligibility.py"}]}}
